articleBody:
- [ ] Subfloor moisture inspection notes — Unchecked subfloor dampness ruins vinyl adhesive and buckles engineered wood.
- [ ] Subfloor levelness check within manufacturer tolerance — High spots and dips cause floating floor joints to flex, separate, and break.
- [ ] Appliance height and clearance measurements — Failing to account for added floor height can trap your dishwasher under the existing countertop.
- [ ] Baseboard and shoe moulding replacement strategy — Removing or undercutting moulding creates clean perimeter edges and protects expansion gaps.
- [ ] Transition strips for adjoining rooms — Differing floor heights between your kitchen and living area require dedicated transition profiles to eliminate trip hazards.
- [ ] Acclimation time verification for materials — Hardwood and certain vinyls require resting on-site before installation to prevent post-install shrinkage or buckling.
- [ ] Dedicated curing schedule for tile thinset and grout — Walking on uncured tile or loading heavy refrigerators too early cracks fresh grout lines and loosens thinset.
- [ ] Appliance disconnection and reconnection plan — Proper shutoffs and re-plumbing for ice makers and dishwashers prevent sudden post-install leaks.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through each item with your estimator before signing your contract. A solid remodeling plan clarifies subfloor prep, material handling, and appliance movement in writing before demolition starts.

When you notice structural deflection, rotted subfloor panels near the sink, or complex room transitions, working with an experienced local contractor is key. Call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 to evaluate your kitchen flooring installation in detail.
